author: C
html: Don’t be discouraged by any negative comments or cheaters Dr. Widom. The class was excellent – I completed it (without a perfect score 🙂 ) and found it to be the best technical education course I have ever had.

author: Alok
html:
I was one of the people who took the course and could not thank you (and the staff) enough for the wonderful course, yet will do so on every opportunity!

An interesting thing from the course also was how the gap between eager-beavers and deadline-driven people widened as the course went along. This caused not only undue pressure on some of us during some of the weeks, the forum discussions also bifurcated correspondingly, making it harder for people to find questions relevant to them. I find it a pity that some of the new courses are still not catering to this issue as they have put several weeks of videos online ahead of time!

html:

author: Ariel
html: Thank you for all your time and effort! The class was great.

author: Henrik Warne
html:

author: Kalpana Mohan
html:
Hi Jennifer, I’m wowed! What a lot of work but how satisfying to have been able to teach so many people in one shot. Thanks for sharing this. I’ll tell Mohan and Parthiv to read this post.
Why don’t you ask the Stanford Magazine to repost this piece on its site? You’ll get a lot more readers that way. Since you’ve done such a nice job of writing it up, I think you should get more mileage out of it.

Kalpana

author: Pervys Rengifo Rengifo
html:
Thank Teacher: In Colombia, many people took this course and the comments I have received have been excellent. I signed on track at the end of last year and I have been very helpful, all materials and activities available in the self-service arrangement. I had the opportunity to take the course in Machine Learning (Andrew Ng) and Introduction to Artificial Intelligence (Norvig and Sebastian Thrun Piter), and the result was a very enriching experience, with teachers who were very generous with knowledge. I learned a lot. I have a blog in Spanish, which I mentioned my experience:
http://pervys-cienciaytecnologia.blogspot.com/2012/01/cursos-gratis-en-la-universidad-de.html
Thank you very much and I will be attentive to the new edition of her courses Introduction to databases.

author: Tony Sidaway
html: Well done Dr Widom. I’m glad your Stanford students also appreciated the hard work and great organizing abilities you brought to this new mode of teaching. I’ll be sure to recommend your course in Autumn, as a professional who has worked with databases to DBA and architect level but still learned much from your free online course.

author: Dan Scott
html:
Jennifer, Thank you. I took the other two classes since I first built my own database (hashing algorithms and all) in 1974 and have taught and used databases ever since. My experiences in the other classes fall into the “almost in tears in gratitude” side of the spectrum. After 44 years as an IT professional it is wonderful to be so excited about my profession again.

As for the teaching modality — no question. The rest of the world will absolutely have to adapt or it will be trampled in the stampede as people worldwide experience the power and sheer joy of learning in the “flipped classroom.” And I agree that the Stanfords and MITs of the world have nothing to fear as long as professors like you leverage the ability to go beyond the simple mastery of material.

author: Marina Chernyavskaya
html: Thank you again, Prof.Widom, for this excellent course! I’m so proud to have been among those first 100 000 students on 2011 online course.
